semantics.requestConcurrency: maximum concurrent admitted HTTP request lifetimes per actor
semantics.messageConcurrency: maximum concurrent message lifetimes per request
semantics.actorExecution: at most one physical guest turn executing per actor incarnation
semantics.serial: exactly one admitted request lifetime and one message lifetime
semantics.gracefulDrain: Seal new HTTP request admissions; keep previously admitted request capabilities available for their bounded message continuations until response close, timeout or explicit cancellation.
semantics.forcedStop: Seal both request and message admission and cancel unfinished logical work; a physical carrier still inside the guest cannot be finalized or recycled until it exits.
semantics.dispatchHandoff: An accepted HTTP exchange holds a non-reusable dispatch-handoff lease from worker selection through actor attachment, including timeout and cancellation. Unpooled actor physical exit remains a separate retirement condition; pooled worker physical quiescence is a separate listener-shutdown condition.
semantics.listenerCarrierBarrier: After sealing listener admission and physically stopping the HTTP transport, success also requires every accepted exchange retired, all exchange-completion Future callbacks returned, and every pooled actor incarnation serving that listener to have exited its physical TurnExecutor boundary with no previously admitted mail or suspended guest receive. Polling is a host-only point-in-time observation and must fail with a bounded explicit timeout rather than certifying stalled carriers.
semantics.forceCloseArbitration: Forced listener close has a single winning owner, fails any unresolved graceful-drain Future, and publishes pending accept failure only outside listener and global HTTP runtime monitors; no false success on cleanup failure or deadline expiry.
semantics.pooledWorkerAdmissionFence: Each pooled worker incarnation has a synchronized, linearizable admission seal. Every accepted HTTP dispatch reserves a handoff before actor selection and releases it in all exit paths. Listener shutdown seals every historically associated incarnation before physical observation; post-seal requests, including concurrent requests from other live listeners sharing a Handler, must use a replacement actor generation. Shutdown waits for all pre-seal handoffs, then requests ActorRuntime.gracefulStop to seal actor-mailbox admission, and requires actual physical carrier exit after terminal DONE publication and thread-local cleanup.
semantics.unpooledPhysicalRetirement: For unpooled HTTP actor requests, a completed actor DONE Future is insufficient to recycle request admission: asynchronous host-only ActorRuntime.httpCarrierQuiescent must establish final physical TurnExecutor and ThreadLocal exit, then State.release may publish the completion callback. Polling and DONE subscribers may not execute guest code or block under the State/ActorRuntime lifecycle monitors. A failed or unavailable physical receipt cannot be treated as success.
semantics.poolGenerationRetirement: Closing a pooled HTTP handler must seal and cancel every historical actor incarnation, including stopped or sealed generations no longer present in the current slot array. Registering a new incarnation races pool stop under a single lock; no generation can appear after the stop snapshot. Registry retirement is permitted only after the actor's physical carrier exit and every listener association has been detached. A failure to cancel one generation must not prevent canceling the others.
semantics.sharedPoolCrossListenerShutdown: If a worker generation has historical associations with two live HTTP listeners, stopping one listener may not close the other listener's actor mailbox or cancel its in-flight guest work. Java currently fails the first listener's independent physical drain explicitly while a second listener retains association, then continues to accept requests on a replacement generation. This is a fail-closed interim safety gate, NOT completed independent per-listener shutdown support or five-backend parity. A full solution requires separate listener ownership or a validated per-listener work-completion lease.

cases.name: serial-alias
cases.oracle: The serial HTTP declaration and explicit (1,1) configuration lower to equivalent immutable HTTP actor policy metadata; aliases survive annotation expansion and tree shaking.

cases.name: nonserial-denial
cases.oracle: A (3,4) configuration may parse, but must fail with a compiler-owned unsupported capability diagnostic until runtime admission, state loans and guest reentry are implemented. Never silently clamp to (1,1).

cases.name: invalid-limits
cases.oracle: Zero, negative, nonliteral, duplicate and conflicting requestConcurrency/messageConcurrency declarations fail before any actor or socket is published.

cases.name: unbound-transport
cases.oracle: A generic mailbox spawn of an HTTP actor without a bound HTTP transport adapter fails closed; no silent ordinary actor fallback.

cases.name: two-level-lifetimes
cases.oracle: Request and per-request message lifetime reservations obey their separate limits; concurrent lifetimes never imply two physical executing guest turns on one actor incarnation.

cases.name: suspend-cancel-reentry
cases.oracle: Suspension retains logical admission while allowing physical carrier release; cancellation/timeout cannot release an exchange during dispatch worker selection or actor handoff, prevents stale continuation reentry, and keeps sealed-state loans exclusive.

cases.name: exchange-incarnation
cases.oracle: Request/exchange authority is one-shot and bound to exact scheduler domain, actor slot and incarnation plus exchange generation; stale, wrong actor, and double claims reject.

cases.name: shutdown-physical-exit
cases.oracle: Graceful listener drain seals request admission, tracks exact worker generations and in-flight handoff leases, then seals every pooled actor mailbox and requires terminal physical carrier exit. A second still-open listener must replace a sealed generation. A DONE Future whose subscriber still owns the carrier cannot certify quiescence; stall or incomplete cleanup yields bounded failure, never false success. An unpooled request cannot retire after DONE alone: terminal physical carrier exit must be observed before releasing its HTTP permit. Shared pooled actors may not be globally stopped by one listener while another still owns them; the current Java interim must fail that listener's drain explicitly rather than cancel the other listener's work.

cases.name: shutdown-failure
cases.oracle: Deadline expiry reports explicit failure; forced stop seals both admission classes and logically cancels remaining requests, but keeps any active physical carrier pending. Concurrent retries and double claims never finalize or report false success.

cases.name: demo-admission-restart
cases.oracle: The unchanged REST demo uses its single admitted request until actor completion, exposes explicit overload behavior, retains persisted state through normal restart and distinguishes termination from graceful draining.

cases.name: aot-provenance
cases.oracle: Each claimed backend compiles the unchanged canonical HTTP actor guest, executes real loopback HTTP, records exact source+compiler+artifact identity and verifies Native AOT/full-AOT where applicable.
